main_body: grey stone mortar bowl with a light rim, green paste visible inside, and a brown pestle leaning out to the upper right
top_band: light grey rim ellipse with green paste interior, rows ~7-10; the rim highlight is lightest on the left
evidence: Reading down the middle column: pestle and green paste in the opening at rows ~7-9, then the light front rim at about row 10, then the darker grey bowl body at rows 10-14, with a dark base below. The oval opening with green contents reads as a surface seen from above, and the rounded bowl front sits below it. This is a correct 3/4 container, though a small one.

style.evidence: The grey bowl body is a few flat bands with little grain or per-stone variation. The green paste and brown pestle each have only about 3 tones. The outline is a dark blue-grey that leans near-black in places, which gives a slightly sticker-like edge. Tiles carry roughly 3-5 colours, well below the reference stall and well, which have scallops, grain and speckle. It is cleanly drawn but thinner and flatter than the Beodeul pieces.
